grandparents_cupboard.reason: Smoked mackerel, crème fraîche, horseradish sauce, lemon and fresh vegetables are all traditional kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco or any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a knife, board, bowl, fork and grater, and the techniques are flaking, chopping and mashing.

works.reason: 200g mackerel with 150g crème fraîche and 80g watercress makes a well-balanced dip for four as a snack, the plentiful crudités suit it, and the salty fish means no added salt is needed.

honest_times.reason: Flaking the fish, chopping the watercress, zesting and cutting four kinds of crudités fits within about 15 minutes for a normal cook, and no cooking is required.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps under its true name, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Watercress is chopped through the dip and used as a topping, so it is central rather than a garnish, and a no-cook snack suits late September.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with no restaurant jargon or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oily fish with a generous plate of raw vegetables makes a satisfying, real-food snack a family would enjoy.
